contribution.position: I hold my earlier position. I am answering qa's claim on axis:risk that cold_start is 600ms, comfortably inside the 800ms budget. The only perf artifact, artifact:perf-report, says cold_start was measured at 1900ms at peak load against an 800ms budget. No 600ms figure appears in any listed artifact. Either qa is citing a different run, such as a non-peak or warm-cache measurement that is not in the artifact list, or the number is wrong. Until that run is provided with its load conditions, the 600ms figure should not offset the 1900ms peak measurement. The comparison that matters for a cache warmer is the peak one. I also note the limits of my own case. artifact:incident-log shows two sev2 incidents from retry storms but does not link them to cold start, so the amplification path is a hypothesis and not an established cause. That is why the evidence request stays open and I am not claiming a proven defect. Product's cost point (artifact:cost-sheet, +3% against a 5% ceiling) and ops' point (artifact:ops-runbook v4 covers deploy and rollback) look sound on their own axes, but neither addresses peak-load latency or retry behavior. artifact:test-report (412 passed, 87% coverage) shows functional correctness only. Still needed: a peak-load run showing cold_start within budget or a documented waiver, plus retry and backoff behavior under peak load that rules out a repeat of the retry storms.
